title.rendered: I Thank My God for You: Gratitude for the People in Our Lives | The Thankful Heart, Day 13

excerpt.rendered: Philippians 1:3-6: Paul thanked God upon every remembrance of his friends. Day 13 of The Thankful Heart gives thanks for the people in our lives.

content.rendered:
Paul wrote this letter from a prison cell, and the first thing he did was thank God for his friends. Some of the greatest gifts God gives us come with names and faces.

The Gospel For Today | Friday, November 27, 2026 | The Thankful Heart, Day 13

Today’s Scripture

“I thank my God upon every remembrance of you, always in every prayer of mine making request for you all with joy, for your fellowship in the gospel from the first day until now, being confident of this very thing, that He who has begun a good work in you will complete it until the day of Jesus Christ.”
Philippians 1:3-6 (NKJV)

Today’s Message

For twelve days we have thanked God for who He is and what He has done. Today we turn to one of His most tender gifts: people. Paul opens his letter to the Philippians with these words: “I thank my God upon every remembrance of you.” Every time their faces came to mind, thanks rose in his heart.

Think about who those people were. Lydia, the businesswoman who opened her home. The jailer who had once locked Paul in stocks and then washed his wounds. A church that had sent gifts to support him again and again (Philippians 4:15-16). They were not perfect people. Later in the same letter Paul has to ask two women in the church to agree with each other. But when Paul remembered them, he did not start with their faults. He started with thanks.

Notice what Paul was thankful for: “your fellowship in the gospel from the first day until now.” These were partners. The word translated “fellowship” is the Greek koinōnia (κοινωνία). In English, fellowship can sound like friendly time together after a service, but koinōnia means partnership, a real sharing in something held in common. That is why the ESV renders it “partnership” here. The Philippians were not spectators of Paul’s ministry; they were sharers in it. They had stood with him in the work of the gospel through hard times and good. And Paul was not only thankful for what they had done. He was confident about what God was still doing in them: “He who has begun a good work in you will complete it.” Thanksgiving for people includes trusting God with their unfinished parts.

Who are the people God has placed in your life? The parent who prayed for you. The friend in Nairobi who called at the right moment. The pastor in Sao Paulo who taught you the Word. The colleague in Dubai who covered for you when you were struggling. The brother or sister in Christ who is still a work in progress, just like you. Each of them is a gift from the same generous hand.

So here is a practice for today. Think of three people and thank God for them by name. Then go one step further: tell them. Send a message, make a call, write a note. Say, “I thank my God for you.” You may never know how much those words will mean. Gratitude for people becomes a gift when it is spoken.

How the Thankful Heart Sees People

It remembers with thanks, not with a list of faults. Paul thanked God upon every remembrance of his friends.

It honours partnership. Fellowship in the gospel is a gift worth naming.

It trusts God with the unfinished parts. He who began a good work will complete it.

Declaration

Lord, I thank You for the people You have placed in my life. I thank my God upon every remembrance of them (Philippians 1:3). I thank You for every friend, family member and partner in the gospel who has walked with me. I am confident that You who began a good work in them, and in me, will complete it until the day of Jesus Christ (Philippians 1:6). I thank You that we are one body in Christ, and that every one of them is a gift from You. In Jesus’ name. Amen.
